title.narrative: Multi Sectoral Lean Season Response to Vulnerable Population in Borno (Dikwa and Jere LGA) and Yobe (Gujba and Nguru LGA)

description.narrative: ltpgtNortheast (BAY states) Nigeria is the epicenter of a deepening humanitarian catastrophe, where the compounding effects of protracted conflict, severe food insecurity, and a collapsed public health environment are creating a lethal crisis for millions. Borno State, is facing a deepening humanitarian crisis where conflict, displacement, economic shocks, and climate disasters converge to drive food insecurity, malnutrition, and dire WASH needs. The March 2025 Cadre Harmonisé projects that 4.6 million people in the BAY states will face crisis or emergency food insecurity during the lean season, while 2.6 million children under five will suffer acute malnutrition, including 1 million at risk of SAM. In Borno, GAM prevalence stands at 15.7% (critical), exceeding WHO’s “very high” threshold, with poor child feeding, low immunization, and frequent disease outbreaks compounding risks. ltbrgtThis nutritional collapse is also propelled by a critical WASH crisis. Recent assessments indicate that 4.4 million people in the northeast are in dire need of WASH assistance (OCHA, 2024), with over 1.6 million Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Borno state alone lacking access to safe water and adequate sanitation (UNICEF, 2024). This infrastructure deficit is a primary driver of illness, with the prevalence of diarrhea in children under five exceeding 30% in high-risk areas (WASH Sector, 2024). recent assessments also show that 73.5% of households lack daily safe water access, 85% lack adequate sanitation, and 82% lack soap, leaving communities vulnerable to cholera and other waterborne diseases. Despite some state and partner interventions such as solar-powered boreholes gaps remain immense, particularly in LGAs like Mafa, Dikwa, and Bama, which host large displaced populations. Macro-economic shocks, including rampant inflation and climate-induced floods that destroyed vast swathes of farmland, have further crippled household resilience. Persistent violence continues to hinder both agricultural activity and humanitarian access, leaving communities isolated and without support. ltbrgtAgainst this backdrop, Smiling Heart Initiative (SHI) in consortium with Pinnacle of Aid Relief Organization (P-Aid), Center for Child Care and Human Development (C3HD) and New Foundation for Displaced Persons (NFDP) seeks donor support to scale up integrated Health, Nutrition and WASH interventions in Jere, Dikwa in Borno and Nguru and Gujba LGA in Yobe state, combining lifesaving malnutrition treatment ranging from active case search, Outpatient Therapeutic Prgramme, (OTP) Tom Brown programme, and Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) Intervention, with essential health interventions and emergency water supply, climate-smart sanitation, hygiene promotion, and mainstreaming protection services, to reduce child mortality, curb disease outbreaks, and strengthen resilience in the face of escalating crises.ltbrgtlt/pgt
